Calendar Home Culture Bids/Sales/Proposals Mecosta County EMS Vehicle Storage Building and County Services Building Remodel 14485 Northland Drive, Big Rapids, Michigan 49307 According to the drawings and specifications prepared by: The Design Forum Inc. MacMillan Associates Prein&Newhof PO Box 561 714 East Midland St 3355 Evergreen Dr NW Belmont MI 49306 Bay City, MI 48706 Grand Rapids, MI 616.454.1398 989.894.4300 616.364.8491 mbelisle@thedesignforum.com jgourd@macmillanassociates.com jmiller@preinnewhof.com Including, but not limited to: site work, site utilities, 4658 SF pole barn construction, connecting masonry passage corridor and approximate 4650 SF interior remodel with new and infilled exterior openings. Sealed bids will be received at the EMS offices located at the Mecosta County Services building located at 14485 Northland Drive, until Friday October 30 th , 11am Eastern Time . At that time, bids will be publicly opened. Bids received after the date and time specified will be returned to the bidder, unopened. An optional pre-bid conference will be held Friday October 16 th at 1pm at the Mecosta County Services Building at 14485 Northland Drive. Bidders are strongly encouraged to attend. Much of the renovation work is desired to match existing finishes, patch/repair areas, etc. Bid Documents will be available after 4:00 pm, on Friday October 9, 2026. Bid documents can be transmitted electronically by contacting the owner’s representative via email Jason Kellogg at jkellogg@mecostacounty.org or the architect Michael Belisle at mbelisle@thedesignforum.com . Click on the drawings and Project Manual for the specifics. Note that the owner can vacate the portion of the interior buildout during construction as they can use another property offsite during construction of the pole barn, connecting passageway, and interior buildout. The owner would like to occupy the areas of the existing county services as long as possible with the initial focus of construction on the pole building. Work may commence once the building permit is issued which is anticipated early November. The contractor will need to work with the owner to keep the existing building as operational as possible during construction as other portions of the building will remain in use. The Owner reserves the right to reject any or all bids and to waive irregularity in the bidding or the bidding process and accept the bid that is most advantageous to the Owner. Engineering Services – Mecosta County Parks Commission The Mecosta County Park Commission is requesting proposals from qualified professional engineering firms for Michigan's Dragon Trail at Hardy Dam – Segment 7 Flood Damage Restoration and Hazard Mitigation Project. The project involves engineering services for restoration of flood-related damage resulting from the April 2026 flooding, as well as evaluation and design of hazard mitigation improvements intended to reduce future flood damage. Services include site investigation, surveying, engineering analysis, design, construction plans and specifications, cost estimating, permitting assistance, FEMA coordination, bidding assistance, construction administration, and project closeout. Interested firms should visit Mecosta County’s Parks website for additional details.
